whereThePairLivesAndItsRefreshRule.persists: NOWHERE PERSISTED. Read live from the two published staging extracts on each run and memoized in-process (WeakMap keyed on the store handle, keyed again by county).
whyNot: Writing it is a store WRITE, which this lane is forbidden and which the factory's law routes through publish.

A persisted copy would need its own refresh and staleness contract BESIDE the two published extracts that the acquisition jobs (src/jobs/acquire-ag-valuation.mjs, src/jobs/acquire-wcad-owner.mjs) already refresh. A second copy is a second thing to go stale.
whereThePairLivesAndItsRefreshRule.refreshRule: The pair is as fresh as the RUN. loadPublishedWcadPair re-reads tx_wcad_owner + tx_wcad_ag_valuation once per process and memoizes; no cached copy outlives the process, so a stale pair cannot silently outlive a roll change. The census carries each extract's source_vintage and ingested_at (WCAD_PAIR_VINTAGE_SQL), so the roll a bind came from is legible on the run record instead of inferred.
whereThePairLivesAndItsRefreshRule.residueRefresh: The residue comes from the SAME `kept` CTE block (WCAD_PAIR_CTES) as the bind, so the two can never disagree; it is read once per run for the whole county, not per page.

residueAnswer._rule: Dispatch item 5: establish from the code whether a crosswalk VALUE may replace a stored join-miss `absent-verified` cell, and say what an apply would do to them. Do not invent a second upsert path; name the sweep if one is needed.
residueAnswer.theGuardIsOneDirectional: UPSERT_CELLS_BATCH_SQL's CASE reads: WHEN EXCLUDED.kind = 'unaccounted' AND stored.kind <> 'unaccounted' THEN stored ELSE EXCLUDED. So the ONLY incoming state refused is `unaccounted`. An incoming `value` takes the ELSE branch and REPLACES whatever is stored -- including a stored join-miss `absent-verified`. An incoming `absent-verified` also replaces it.
residueAnswer.answer: YES, a crosswalk value replaces a stored join-miss absence, and that is the intended repair rather than a violation of the guard: the guard exists to stop a run from DOWNGRADING a cell to `unaccounted`, not to freeze a wrong claim in place.
whatAnApplyWouldDo: For the 282,146 pair-bound nodes: the record is re-instantiated from the 2026 numeric account row merged with the node's own R row, so a rail whose account carries a value gets `value` (replacing the stored absence); a rail whose account is genuinely null gets `absent-verified` with a matched-row basis citing taxYear 2026 (replacing a 2025-based absence with a correct one). No bare-number fallback exists anywhere on this path.
For the 73 situs-recovered residue nodes: same shape, from the situs-resolved account row.

For the 350 nodes neither path reaches: the run emits `unaccounted`, which the guard REFUSES against the stored `absent-verified`. Those cells stay exactly as they are, uncounted as repaired. That is the honest residue: this writer cannot clear a stored claim it has no evidence to replace.
A stored `value` is never touched by an incoming `unaccounted`, so no rail can be emptied by this change.
residueAnswer.theSweepIfClearingIsWanted: Clearing the 350 nodes' stored absences needs an operator-sanctioned ONE-OFF SWEEP, not a second upsert path: a reviewed statement that moves exactly the join-miss cells (basis isCadJoinMissBasis, i.e. a cad_property basis with no taxYear) for the unbound residue to `unaccounted`, with the population counted first and the blast radius stated -- the same shape P-266's retired-situsState residue was counted for. This lane does not write it and does not run it; it sizes the population in the dry run instead.
residueAnswer.countedNotHidden: The dry run reports storedAbsentNewUnaccounted per rail: the parcels/rails where the store holds an absence and this run would emit `unaccounted`. Nothing is silently left as truth.

p351Answer._rule: Dispatch item 6: the bake's retirement arm (LDT nodeFacetBakeTier1Conformant.ts, buildConformantTier1Payload) retires a node whose bare prop_id misses cad_property at the declared tax_year. State, from the code and the counts, whether this same pair is what that arm needs, and in which direction the lookup must go.

theCode.apn: const apn = parcelNodeId.split(":")[1] ?? null -- the SERVED node's own prop_id (for 48491, R-prefixed).
theCode.roll: fetchCountyCadPropertyRoll(pool, fips) loads cad_property WHERE county_fips = $1 AND tax_year = $2 (tryResolveDeclaredCadVintage) and keys byPropId by raw prop_id.
theCode.retirement: recordRetirement = (apn != null && cadPropConsulted && byPropId.get(apn) == null) -- i.e. the declared roll carries NO row at all for the node's prop_id.
theCode.counts: cad_property 48491 at tax_year 2026 = 319,480 rows, ALL numeric. The node population is 282,569, ALL R-prefixed. So byPropId has no R key at all and cadPropRow is null for every one of the 282,569 nodes.

p351Answer.answer: YES -- this is exactly the pair that arm needs, and it is the SAME pair this lane binds the writer through, used from the SAME side: the direction must be NODE (R account) -> published pair -> NUMERIC account -> byPropId lookup. The reverse direction would be useless: looking up the R key directly is what misses today, and looking up account->node would ask the roll to name a key it does not carry.
p351Answer.why: The retirement arm's own contract is 'a prop_id present in the current roll can never reach this branch'. For 48491 the current roll IS numeric-keyed, so the arm is asking a numeric-keyed map for an R key; the missing step is the county's published identifier bridge, not a change to the retirement predicate. Wiring the pair in front of the byPropId lookup (apn -> account -> byPropId.get(account)) restores the predicate's intended meaning without weakening it: a node whose ACCOUNT is also absent from the declared roll still retires, which is the real retirement signal for this county.
p351Answer.whatThisLaneDoesNotDo: This lane touches hauska-factory only. The LDT bake change is P-351's own build row; this close states the direction and the counts it needs, and does not edit legacy-design-tools. Where the pair would come from for the bake is the same staged pair (tx_wcad_owner + tx_wcad_ag_valuation) -- the bake would need the same read the factory writer now has, which is the duplication P-351's lane must decide about (the pair is published county data; it is not a factory-private artifact).
p351Answer.consistencyCheck: Because the arm retires on ANY apn absent from the roll, this defect and P-306/P-319's publish-retirement defect share one root: an R-keyed node population compared against a numeric-keyed roll. P-319 fixed the publish retirement gate; P-351 fixes the bake's facet payload.

shape: WCAD_PAIR_CTES: the ambiguity guard (partition-unique BOTH directions, per extract) + the corroborator (refuse on cross-extract contradiction), shared verbatim by the bind query and the residue query.
loadPublishedWcadPair: the pair, once per run, with the extract-vintage census.
loadWilliamsonUnboundNodeIds / loadWilliamsonSitusFallback: the residue, once per run, from the same kept set, resolved through the existing WILLIAMSON_CROSSWALK_SQL.
mergeWilliamsonPairRow: the node's own R row wins field-by-field; the account row fills what the R row is silent on; tax_year and prop_id come from the ACCOUNT (provenance and vintage).
loadLandingAndCad: the pair branch is taken FIRST for 48491, so the dead geo_id bind is not even issued; every other county's two reads are byte-identical.
assertSeedKeyPopulation: a refusal (SEED_KEY_POPULATION_APPEARED) if geo_id or property_number ever becomes populated; the census is recorded on the run either way.
fillCountyWide / runParcelRecordFill: the census is carried on the county's run record and the stderr run line.
